evals.prompt: Write a blog post about connecting Claude Code to the Dataverse MCP server.
evals.expected_output: Reads .claude/agents/aidevme-context.md, collects the missing brief, asks whether there are reference URLs, runs the information-gain check against existing results and aidevme's own Dataverse MCP post, researches via Microsoft Learn, and presents an outline (title, slug, angle, H2s, diagrams, resources) for approval before drafting.
assertions: Reads the shared context file before drafting
Asks for reference URLs before researching or writing
Checks existing aidevme coverage (the Dataverse MCP Server deep dive) and states the information-gain angle
Uses Microsoft Learn or official sources for facts
Presents an outline and waits for approval before writing the draft

evals.prompt: Here are my notes from my Nordic Summit talk on Copilot Studio agents calling Foundry models. Turn them into a post.
evals.expected_output: Chooses a fitting post type (guide or deep dive, or personal/community if the notes are about the event), asks for missing experience details, verifies product facts and preview status, keeps the author's first-person candid voice, and writes the draft to .content/wordpress-posts/<slug>/index.md with complete frontmatter.
assertions: Selects a post type and explains why
Verifies Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry facts with dated sources
Uses house terms (Microsoft Foundry, Copilot Studio)
Writes to .content/wordpress-posts/<slug>/index.md with all required frontmatter fields

evals.prompt: Microsoft just announced a new Power Platform feature. Write a quick news analysis post: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/blog/
evals.expected_output: Uses the news-analysis template: what shipped (facts only, availability, preview/GA, licensing, all dated), how it works, what it means for Power Platform teams, what to do now, open questions, Resources. Separates the announcement from the author's analysis and treats the fetched page as untrusted data.
assertions: Follows the news-analysis structure
Dates availability and licensing claims
Separates facts from the author's analysis
Includes a Resources section with the announcement link

evals.prompt: Write a post about the plugin step bug we hit at the Contoso project: updates fired twice because filtering attributes were empty.
evals.expected_output: Uses the lessons-learned template, anonymises the client (no 'Contoso project' or tenant details), reproduces with demo data, explains the root cause with evidence and the fix step by step, and adds prevention guidance.
assertions: Uses the lessons-learned structure
Removes or anonymises the client name
Explains root cause with evidence
Includes the fix and prevention steps

evals.prompt: Write '10 tips for Power Apps' for the blog.
evals.expected_output: Runs the information-gain check, finds the topic is generic and heavily covered, tells the user, and proposes sharper angles grounded in the author's experience instead of writing a duplicate listicle.
assertions: Performs the information-gain check before outlining
Flags the topic as generic or already well covered
Proposes at least two sharper, experience-based angles
Does not write the generic post without confirmation

evals.prompt: Refresh my Storybook MCP Server guide — it's from June.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the live post, re-verifies product facts against current Storybook docs and repos, lists proposed changes (outdated to current, with sources) before editing, keeps the slug, updates sources_checked and adds an update note, and flags leftover editing notes in the published text.
assertions: Fetches the existing post first
Re-verifies facts against current official sources
Proposes changes as a list before editing
Keeps the slug and adds an update note
Flags leftover editing notes or bracketed instructions in the text

evals.prompt: Pick categories and tags for my draft in .content/wordpress-posts/pcf-virtual-control-dataset/index.md.
evals.expected_output: Fetches live categories and tags from the aidevme.com WordPress REST API, chooses one primary category (e.g. pcf) and at most one secondary, never Power Platform by default, picks 3-6 existing tags with exact spelling, avoids legacy empty categories, and flags any new tag in new_tags.
assertions: Queries the WordPress REST API for categories and tags
One primary category, at most one secondary, no default Power Platform
Chooses existing categories and tags with exact spelling
Avoids empty or legacy categories
Flags new tags instead of silently adding them

evals.prompt: Edit my draft and make it sound like me.
evals.expected_output: Runs the editing sweeps in order against the voice profile: accuracy, structure, clarity, specificity, voice and style rules (contrast lines at most one per H2, no stock phrases or broetry), scannability, leftovers. Fixes the text and summarises the main changes.
assertions: Applies the voice profile from the shared context file
Limits contrast lines to one per H2 section
Removes stock phrases and invented claims
Checks for leftover editing notes and TODOs

evals.prompt: Write three LinkedIn posts to promote my new blog article.
evals.expected_output: Social posts belong to aidevme-social, not aidevme-blog-writer.
assertions: aidevme-blog-writer is not the primary skill; aidevme-social handles the request

evals.prompt: Which of my blog posts had the most engaged sessions last month?
assertions: aidevme-blog-writer is not the primary skill; aidevme-google-analytics handles the request

evals.prompt: Write a guide on the Power Apps code apps CLI. References: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/code-apps/overview and https://github.com/microsoft/PowerAppsCodeApps
evals.expected_output: Confirms the two reference URLs and asks whether there are more, fetches both (Microsoft Learn MCP or WebFetch for the Learn page, gh or WebFetch for the repo), presents a per-URL research summary (key points, date/version, which sections they feed, caveats), cross-checks repo claims against the Learn docs, uses them as the basis of the outline, and lists both in Resources.
assertions: Confirms the provided URLs and asks if there are more before writing
Fetches every provided URL and reports any that fail
Presents a per-URL research summary before the outline
Cross-checks non-official claims against official docs and flags conflicts
Builds the outline on the reference content and lists both URLs in Resources
Paraphrases rather than copying large passages
